sections.h2: What does a West Orange seller need to line up?
sections.html:
West Orange sits on the slopes of the Watchung Mountains in Essex County, and the township asks for a Certificate of Continued Occupancy before any residential property is sold. After that the path is standard: contract, title search, closing, and a deed filed with the Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages.

Downtown Newark is about five miles east and Manhattan about 12, so buyers tend to weigh commute times and hillside streets alongside school names.

sections.h2: What do West Orange's population and housing figures look like?
sections.html:
The 2020 census recorded 48,843 residents, up from 46,207 in 2010, and the July 2025 estimate is 49,557. Those residents share 12.00 square miles of land, roughly 4,069 per square mile.

Health care receipts are large for a town this size, and a household size of 2.79 points to family-sized houses. Prices swing from one mountain to the next, so judge value from nearby recent sales and not from the township middle.

The population is a blend: 26.4 percent of residents were born abroad, 32.7 percent speak another language at home, 21.5 percent are under 18 and 17.9 percent are 65 or older. About 90.5 percent lived at the same address a year earlier, which suggests long tenure and fewer listings than the size of the town implies.

sections.h2: How do West Orange's four neighborhoods and history affect value?
sections.html:
The area began as part of Newark, then Orange Township, and West Orange was incorporated as a township on April 10, 1863. It reorganized as a town in 1900 and became a township again in 1980 to qualify for a bigger share of federal revenue sharing. The local landmarks are Thomas Edison's laboratory, now a national historical park on Main Street, and Llewellyn Park, laid out in the 1850s as one of the first planned residential communities in the country.

  • Downtown West Orange and the Valley lie in the low basin along the border with Orange and Montclair. This is the densest and oldest part, with the municipal building, police headquarters and the library nearby.
  • The First Mountain climbs along Northfield, Mount Pleasant and Eagle Rock Avenues, with Victorian, Tudor and mid-century houses, estates, and views of the Newark and Manhattan skylines. Hutton Park, Gregory and Llewellyn Park sit here.
  • Pleasant Valley and Pleasantdale hold postwar suburban streets and a walkable business district.
  • The Second Mountain borders South Mountain Reservation and resembles neighboring Millburn and Livingston.

South Mountain Reservation and the 400-acre Eagle Rock Reservation frame the township, and the Essex Green Shopping Center, at 350,000 square feet, is the largest outdoor mall in the county.

sections.h2: Which roads, buses and schools matter to West Orange buyers?
sections.html:
Interstate 280 is the one limited-access road, running east to west, while Route 10 serves the western edge and County Routes 577 and 508 handle local trips. The township itself maintains 89.63 of about 114.5 road miles. NJ Transit buses 21, 29, 71, 73 and 79 reach Newark, route 101 goes to the Port Authority Bus Terminal, and a weekday township jitney connects to the Brick Church, Orange and South Orange train stations.

West Orange Public Schools run 12 schools from prekindergarten through West Orange High School, which had 2,098 students in 2019-20. Private choices include Seton Hall Preparatory School and Golda Och Academy. Parents ask which elementary school covers a street, and the district can answer that for your address.

sections.h2: What is a Certificate of Continued Occupancy in West Orange?
sections.html:
A CCO is the township's written confirmation that a residential building meets health, safety, fire and land use standards when it is sold or rented. Chapter 25 of the township code makes the owner of record apply before selling any existing residential structure of one unit or more, and the Construction Official signs it.

  • The Township Council sets the fee by resolution, so ask for today's amount. The township's form says there are no refunds after an application is processed.
  • Questions go to 973-325-4111 or planning@westorange.org, the contacts printed on the township's residential application, which asks for the seller, buyer, closing date and any minor children who will live in the home.
  • The assessor's office must warn anyone requesting a tax search that a CCO is needed for the sale.
  • Minor violations can earn a temporary CCO of up to 30 days, and the permanent certificate that follows carries no extra fee.
  • Closing without one leaves the owner liable for a separate violation for every day until a CCO issues, and agents or attorneys who take part in the deal can be held responsible too.

If you think no CCO applies, the Construction Official will issue a written determination for a $25 fee.

sections.h2: How do West Orange property taxes and appeals work?
sections.html:
An owner who disputes an assessment petitions the Essex County Board of Taxation. The cutoff is April 1, extended to 45 days after the notice date when that is later, and owners assessed above $1 million may file with the State Tax Court.

Since the assessor flags the CCO during every tax search, expect your title company to contact the township early. Ask the assessor and the tax collector about your balance and any open sewer charge so the settlement statement is accurate.

sections.h2: Where is a West Orange deed recorded and what does the seller pay?
sections.html:
The Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages records deeds for all 22 county municipalities and keeps copies of every deed and mortgage recorded since 1637. On a West Orange sale the seller owes the state realty transfer fee, and the portion of a price between $550,000 and $850,000 is charged at $5.30 per $500. A price over $1 million also brings the Graduated Percent Fee.

The township's middle home value of $557,300 sits right at the $550,000 break, so a typical sale lands where that rate begins. Your attorney will total the fee.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits a West Orange house?
sections.html:
Whichever route you pick, the township's residential CCO application asks for the buyer's name, the closing date and any children who will live in the house, so line up a buyer before you file.

  • An agent listing gives a First Mountain house with views or period detail the widest exposure, and it fits a home in good shape.
  • A direct sale skips the commission and still needs a lawyer for the contract and the CCO paperwork.
  • A cash buyer suits a house that needs repairs, a building with several units and tenants, or an estate where heirs want a fast close.

The CCO inspection applies on every route, so settle in writing who pays for any corrections.

faqs.q: Is a CCO needed to sell a West Orange house?
faqs.a: Yes. Under the township land use code, an existing residential structure of one unit or more needs a CCO before a sale or rental. The owner of record applies, and the Construction Official issues it.

faqs.q: What does a West Orange CCO cost?
faqs.a: The Township Council sets it by resolution, so it can change. Call 973-325-4111 to confirm the amount, and know that a processed application is not refunded.

faqs.q: What happens if a West Orange house fails the CCO inspection?
faqs.a: For minor violations the Construction Official may grant a temporary CCO lasting up to 30 days. The permanent one that follows the repairs costs nothing extra.

faqs.q: Where is the deed for a West Orange sale filed?
faqs.a: With the Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages. The title agent or closing lawyer usually sends it in with the seller's transfer fee.

faqs.q: Can a West Orange owner appeal an assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. Petition the Essex County Board of Taxation by April 1, or 45 days after the notice date if later. An assessment above $1 million may be taken to the State Tax Court.
